display.purpose: Hero headline, section headlines, card/testimonial titles. Never used for body copy.

body.purpose: All paragraph copy, labels, and form fields. Never lighter than semibold (600).

shadows.name: button-press
shadows.purpose: Flat offset shadow under primary buttons at rest; compresses to 0 3px 0 on hover/press.

shadows.name: card-flat
shadows.purpose: Flat offset shadow under service cards at rest.

motion.name: float-y
motion.purpose: Ambient vertical drift for large decorative blobs.

motion.name: float-y2
motion.purpose: Ambient vertical drift, inverse phase, for a second blob layer.

motion.name: wiggle
motion.purpose: Slow rotation wiggle for small decorative squares.

motion.name: pop-in
motion.purpose: Entrance animation for hero content: fade + rise + scale.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main call-to-action button (e.g. "Book a Free Chat"). Pill-shaped, flat offset shadow, presses down on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-block; background: #e76943; color: #ffffff; font-weight: 800; font-size: 18px; padding: 16px 32px; border-radius: 9999px; text-decoration: none; box-shadow: 0 7px 0 #b6502f; transition: transform 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover, .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { transform: translateY(3px); box-shadow: 0 3px 0 #b6502f; outline: none; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Ghost/outline button (e.g. "See Our Services"). Inverts to solid fill on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-block; background: #ffffff; color: #18765f; font-weight: 800; font-size: 18px; padding: 16px 32px; border-radius: 9999px; border: 3px solid #18765f; text-decoration: none; transition: background 0.2s, color 0.2s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover, .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { background: #18765f; color: #ffffff; outline: none; }

components.name: Eyebrow Badge
components.description: Small rotated pill badge used above headlines and section tags.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: #ffffff; color: #e76943; font-weight: 800; font-size: 13px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04em; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 9999px; transform: rotate(-2deg); } .ds-badge-dot { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #39bf9a; }

components.name: Service Card
components.description: Colored service card with asymmetric torn-corner radius; lifts and rotates on hover.

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Form field used in the contact form (name, grade, message).
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; background: #ffffff; border: 2px solid #e9ddc8; border-radius: 12px; padding: 14px 16px; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600; color: #18765f; outline: none; transition: border-color 0.15s; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: #18765f; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #9a9184; font-weight: 400; }

narrative.overview:
Bloom Tutoring's interface reads as a garden in bloom: organic blob shapes float and drift behind circular photo frames, leaf-green and marigold-orange sit against a soft cream ground, and everything is built from rounded, growth-shaped forms rather than hard rectangles. The system is warm and reassuring first — nothing sharp, sterile, or clinical is allowed near it — while still projecting the confidence and competence a parent needs to trust a tutor with their child's education through Grade 12 and AP-level work.

The system deliberately avoids two failure modes: the sterile SaaS-dashboard look of generic edtech (no cold grays, no boxy cards, no corporate blue), and cutesy toy-box childishness that would undersell older students' work. It threads that needle with an adult-credible warmth — organic, botanical, hand-tended, but not juvenile.

Components lean bouncy and confident: buttons press down on hover, cards lift and tilt slightly, decorative shapes float and wiggle continuously at low opacity. The palette is a garden bed, not a classroom poster — leaf-green and sprout-mint as growth colors, marigold-orange and peach-bloom as bloom colors, cream as the soil/paper ground.
keyCharacteristics: Organic blob and circle forms over rectangles wherever a shape is decorative or photographic.
Warm, growth-themed palette: greens/mints for trust and stability, orange/peach for warmth and action.
Rounded, chunky display type (Baloo 2) paired with a friendly, readable body face (Nunito).
Continuous low-amplitude ambient motion (floating blobs, wiggling squares) that never demands attention.
Bold, forceful primary color blocking on cards and buttons — color carries hierarchy more than size does.

rules.name: The Single Orange Rule
rules.body: Marigold Orange appears only on things a visitor can act on (buttons, the CTA badge, the enquiry send button). It never appears as decoration or section background — if a user sees orange, it's clickable.

rules.name: The No-Light-Text Rule
rules.body: Body copy is never lighter than semibold (600). Regular weight (400) is reserved for form placeholder text only — every other word on the page is built to feel confidently said, not murmured.

dos: Do keep Marigold Orange exclusive to actionable elements (The Single Orange Rule).
Do use irregular organic border-radius blobs for decorative shapes, not plain circles or rectangles.
Do set body text at semibold (600) or heavier; never use regular-weight paragraph text outside form placeholders.
Do pair every primary button with a physical "press down" hover (translate + shadow compression), not a simple opacity or color fade.
Do keep decorative motion slow, continuous, and low-amplitude (float/wiggle) — never abrupt or attention-grabbing.
donts: Don't introduce cold grays, corporate blues, or hard-edged rectangular cards — they break the garden/growth identity and read as clinical edtech.
Don't push the aesthetic into toy-box childishness (no cartoon mascots, no primary-school clip art); the audience includes parents of Grade 12/AP students.
Don't use soft blurred drop shadows; the system's current depth language is flat color blocking plus solid offset shadows, not ambient blur.
Don't align decorative squares/dots to the grid — they're rotated off-axis on purpose.
Don't fabricate real-sounding testimonial photography or names; the testimonial avatars are intentionally placeholder icons until real photos exist.
